key_insight: Fe dopants and oxygen vacancies make SrTiO3 OER activity strongly Fermi-level dependent, with neutral defects staying near-pristine while reduced defect states can severely worsen overpotential.
engineering_relevance: Defect and Fermi-level engineering can be used to tune perovskite oxide electrocatalysts, but only if charge state, segregation, and surface site effects are considered together.
method: Charge-dependent defect formation and segregation energies plus charge transition levels.
Computational hydrogen electrode free-energy profiles for OER intermediates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantified overpotentials for pristine and defected surfaces, including ~0.43–0.48 V for neutral Fe, up to 1.35 V for reduced Fe states, and up to 2.13 V for oxygen-vacancy states.
watch_item: Predictions depend on assumed defect charge states and surface termination, so real electrodes may deviate if reconstruction, kinetics, or operating conditions shift the Fermi level.
paper_title: Fermi-Level-Dependent Defect Chemistry and Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Fe-Doped and Oxygen-Deficient \ce{SrTiO3}(001)
